name: The Lucavsala Linden

location.address: Lucavsala island, near the monument to Russian soldiers fallen in the Great Northern War

access: Free, public island park with walking trails (Rigas Meži recreation area); reachable on foot
transport: Bus/tram to Kipsala or Torņakalns then walk across the Lucavsala footbridge, approx 15-20 min walk from nearest stop
verify_notes: Latvia's officially designated 'valsts nozīmes dižkoks' (state-significant heritage tree), Riga's thickest and largest linden and among the 2nd-3rd most voluminous trees in the city. Circumference measured 6.82m at 1.2m height in 2009 (up from 5.34m when first measured by Atis Baiža in 1975, so it has been tracked for 50 years, growth consistent with a long-lived specimen). Height 26m, crown area ~350 sqm. Age given as 'approximately 200 years' by dziedava.lv/Guntis Eniņš's tree survey book '100 dižākie un svētākie' (2008), a vague source figure kept as given rather than sharpened. Second source is Riga's own open-data heritage tree register (georiga.eu / data.gov.lv, CC BY 4.0, maintained by Riga's Urban Development Department since 1998), which lists this as a locally/state protected tree; this confirms designation and public standing but the individual downloadable dataset file (SHP/GPKG/KML) was not opened by this pass, only the catalogue page. Coordinates 56°55'31"N 24°7'34"E convert to 56.9253, 24.1261, matching the Wikidata candidate exactly. A rowan shrub grows from the crown fork where the tree branches, a detail worth keeping for the story. Lucavsala is a Daugava river island, now Riga's public forestry-managed recreation area (rigasmezi.lv 'Taka Lucavsalā' trail page); the page itself 403'd on fetch (likely bot-blocking) so trail/access detail is from the URL and site description rather than a direct read, hence flagged rather than fully confirmed on the access side.

name: The Ēbeļmuiža Oak

location.address: Ēbeļmuižas parks, on the grounds of the former Ēbeļmuiža manor, Ziepniekkalns

access: Free, stands in a public park (former manor grounds); no restriction noted
transport: Ziepniekkalns district, Pārdaugava; nearest stop not independently verified this pass
verify_notes: Designated dižkoks (heritage tree), the thickest tree in Pārdaugava (the Daugava's left-bank half of Riga). Quercus robur, 20m tall, girth 5.60m, crown area ~250 sqm, surveyed by dendrologist Atis Baiža. Age given as 'apmēram 300 gadus vecs' (about 300 years old) by Guntis Eniņš's tree survey book '100 dižākie un svētākie' (2008) via Latvian Wikipedia; independently corroborated by Vides Vēstis (Latvian environmental magazine), 'Desmit dižākie koki Rīgā 2009', which gives the identical 5.60m circumference and places it 'Ziepniekkalnā', and notes the trunk has been 'pamatīgi apstrādāts' (heavily treated/repaired) with metal sheets and plates over the decades, though it 'vēl kuplo un zaļo' (still thrives and is green) as of that 2009 survey. Supports (balsti) added and surroundings tidied in 2000. Address discrepancy worth flagging for the writer: the tree's own Wikipedia infobox coordinate field cites 'Valdeķu iela 54' while the article prose gives 'Zaļenieku iela 21' as the park/manor address; both streets sit in the same Ziepniekkalns area and the coordinate (56.9053, 24.0987, matching the Wikidata candidate exactly) is treated as ground truth rather than either street number. No source found more recent than the 2008/2009 pair, so flagged for lack of a post-2010 confirmation of continued life, and for the address discrepancy above.

name: The Kaltiņi Oak

location.address: Berģu iela 160, by Mašēnu Lake, near Riga's eastern city boundary

access: Free, stands beside a former/current social care centre ('Ezerkrasti') by the lake; publicly reachable, no gate or entry fee noted in sources
transport: Eastern edge of Riga administrative territory (roughly 13km from the city centre by straight line); address is within Riga city limits, but nearest stop/route not independently verified this pass
verify_notes: Designated dižkoks, described by Vides Vēstis (2009 survey) as the thickest tree in all of Riga (6.80m circumference measured then). Latvian Wikipedia (citing Eniņš's 2008 book) gives 6.85m, so the two independent sources are in close agreement (5cm apart, consistent with continued growth or normal measurement variance). Quercus robur, 22m tall, crown area ~190 sqm. Age given as 'apmēram 330 gadus vecs' as a vague source figure, kept as given. First mentioned in the press in 1964 by S. Saliņš. Notable history: the trunk cavity was deliberately set on fire three times in 1967 by unknown parties, then sealed in 1968; the tree has been under state protection since 1977; in 1981 a sewage treatment plant was being built for a nearby care home right next to the oak, and the project was changed to spare it thanks to intervention by dendrologist/journalist Guntis Eniņš. A rare, EU-protected fungus, zeltpore (Hapalopilus croceus), grows in the trunk hollow, a strong detail for the story. No source found more recent than 2009-2015, so flagged for lack of a post-2015 confirmation of continued life; address is administratively within Riga (per both sources) despite sitting near the city's eastern edge, so it is treated as an in-city tree rather than a day-trip entry.

name: The Zasulauks Maple

location.address: Kuldīgas iela 31/33 (the same building is also addressed as Kalnciema iela 31/33), Zasulauks

access: Free, grows beside a historic wooden tenement building in the Kalnciema Quarter (Kalnciema kvartāls), a public heritage and market district; visible from the street
transport: Zasulauks neighbourhood, close to Riga centre; nearest stop not independently verified this pass
verify_notes: The thickest and most spreading maple in Riga, and either the second-thickest (per dziedava.lv) or fourth-largest (per dabasretumi.lv) maple in Latvia. Acer platanoides, 26m tall, crown area ~450 sqm, trunk forks into two stems at 2.5m height. Girth given as 5.3-5.4m by Latvian Wikipedia (citing Eniņš 2008 and dziedava.lv) and independently corroborated at 5.34m by Vides Vēstis' 2009 'Desmit dižākie koki Rīgā' survey, an exact match with the lower figure. First measured by dendrologist Atis Baiža in 1975 at 4m girth, so it has grown roughly 1.3-1.4m in circumference over 34 years, tracked evidence of a living, growing tree rather than a static registry entry. Age given as 'apmēram 140 gadus vecs', a vague source figure kept as given. Stands in the former grounds of Zasumuiža manor. Address discrepancy worth flagging: the tree's own article gives Kuldīgas iela 31/33, while the separate 'Kalnciema iela' heritage-buildings article lists a 'koka īres nams' (wooden tenement building) at Kalnciema iela 31/33 with this same maple beside it; almost certainly the same corner building addressed differently per street, and the Kalnciema Quarter is itself a well-known, publicly walkable heritage and market area, which supports (without fully proving) that the tree stands where the public can see it rather than in an enclosed private courtyard. No source found more recent than 2009-2015, so flagged for lack of a post-2015 confirmation of continued life.

name: The Kanālmalas Oak

location.address: Kanālmalas apstādījumi (City Canal gardens), central Riga, near the Freedom Monument and the Laima Clock

access: Free, stands in Riga's central public canal-park (Kanālmalas apstādījumi), open at all times, no restriction
transport: In the very centre of Riga, a few minutes' walk from the Freedom Monument; any central bus/tram/trolleybus stop serves it
verify_notes: This Wikidata candidate (Q54292991) has no Wikipedia article and no name of its own; identified from its raw Wikidata claims: P10241 (individual of taxon) points to Quercus robur, P625 gives the coordinate 56.950294/24.113493 (in central Riga's Kanālmalas apstādījumi park, right by the Freedom Monument/Laima Clock), P31 classes it as a Wikidata 'remarkable tree', and its P18 image is a Commons file titled 'Koks Kanālmalas apstādījumos' ('Tree in the Canal Gardens plantings'). That Commons file's own description (source 1 above) reads 'aizsargājams koks Kanālmalas apstādījumos, Rīgā' (a PROTECTED tree in the Canal Gardens, Riga), was photographed 2018-05-20 by a named contributor for the 'Wiki Loves Earth 2018 in Latvia' campaign (a photo contest specifically documenting Latvia's state-registered protected natural objects/dižkoki), and carries a field GPS reading rather than a digitised address, which is why location_precision is confirmed. Second, independent source: an LSM.lv (Latvian Public Media) feature on the history of the Kanālmalas apstādījumi park quotes a Rīgas Meži park-management source saying rhododendrons have thrived there and 'ir arī divi veci ozoli, kas arī varētu būt no Kūfalta laikiem' (there are also two old oaks, which could also date from [landscape architect Georgs] Kūfalts' time, i.e. the 1880s), giving a possible but hedged age basis of roughly 140 years; the article does not name or pinpoint either oak individually, so this pass cannot be certain the Wikidata-tagged tree is one of the 'two old oaks' described, only that the identification (a protected old oak standing in this exact park) is consistent across both sources. Flagged for that reason, for the unhedged age, and for having no dedicated write-up anywhere. No girth or height figure found in either source. This is the most central and most easily reached candidate of the batch, a short walk from the Freedom Monument.
